risks.title: Cyberattacks compromising sensitive data
risks.summary: A cyberattack could compromise sensitive client or patient data, leading to financial, legal, and reputational losses.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is at the top of risk factors and described as existential. The language is strong (risks associated with cyber threats). Dedicated governance (SPPO, audit committee) and quarterly board updates indicate high severity. Cybersecurity category heavily weighted. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
risks.summary: Failure to comply with strict data protection laws (such as GDPR or HIPAA) could result in heavy fines and damage client trust.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is closely tied to cybersecurity and personal data. Repeated mention of GDPR, HIPAA compliance, etc. The role of the DPO (30 years of experience) underscores importance. Language affirming compliance obligations and risks of sanctions. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on key personnel expertise in cybersecurity
risks.summary: Loss of experienced executives in cybersecurity or data protection could weaken governance and incident response.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of the experience of the Head of IT (30 years) and the DPO (13 years at Certara). Their central role in cyber governance and compliance indicates critical dependence. High risk but mitigated by SPPO structure. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Operational risks related to IT infrastructures
risks.summary: Failures in computer systems or SaaS platforms could disrupt client services and compromise business continuity.
risks.score_rationale: SaaS technology company managing sensitive data. Text mentions critical SaaS environments running for 16 years. Any technical failure or system outage could interrupt services and harm trust. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Undisclosed legal and contingent risks
risks.summary: Ongoing lawsuits or disputes, even if not detailed, could lead to legal costs and unexpected financial losses.
risks.score_rationale: Reference to Note 11 on litigation, but no detailed information provided. Minimal mention in the 10-K, suggesting a present but not aggravated risk. Category moderately weighted. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Volatility in bookings within the biopharma industry
risks.summary: Fluctuations in demand within the pharmaceutical industry can affect revenue stability and future growth.
risks.score_rationale: Text emphasizes that bookings vary significantly based on biopharma sector health. Explicit mention that bookings do not reliably predict revenue. Recurring and central risk for financial predictability. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Regulatory dependence and authority acceptance
risks.summary: A decline in regulatory support or a policy shift toward biosimulation could reduce demand for Certara's products and services.
risks.score_rationale: Acceptance by regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA) is critical for product and service demand. A reversal in acceptance trends could eliminate or substantially reduce demand for biosimulation services. (default score, to be refined)

ai_positioning.summary: Certara explicitly integrates AI and machine learning into its biosimulation solutions. The approach is centered on an 'expert-in-the-loop' model that deploys AI capabilities within validated scientific frameworks and expert-led workflows, rather than as autonomous automated systems. AI is used to automate biosimulation processes, create generative AI applications for regulatory documents, and enhance productivity and insight generation while maintaining scientific validity and transparency.
evidence: Our technology and scientists incorporate modern advances in scientific understanding, drug research and development experience, data analysis, and AI

Our approach to AI is grounded in our long-standing expertise in mechanistic and empirical modeling. We deploy AI capabilities within validated scientific frameworks and expert-led workflows, rather than as standalone automated systems.
This expert-in-the-loop model allows us to leverage native AI capabilities in a manner that is consistent with regulatory expectations for transparency, reproducibility, and explainability.
Native AI and machine learning technologies are being incorporated across our technology and consulting services portfolios

We are using machine learning to automate and speed the process of biosimulation, and we have created generative AI applications to aid in drafting regulatory documents from scientific analyses and clinical data.
We apply AI capabilities within established modeling environments and under the supervision of experienced scientists and regulatory experts.
